title: Record of Meeting - Community Depository Institutions Advisory Council - April 11, 2024
summary: The Community Depository Institutions Advisory Council met on April 11, 2024, noting that the economy remains resilient but faces persistent inflationary pressures, with inflation hurting low- and moderate-income families most. Council members reported that goods inflation is slowing while services inflation persists due to labor costs. Housing affordability remains a challenge across Districts, and labor markets remain tight, though pay increases have moderated from 6-7% last year to 4-5% in 2024.
key_points: Economy remains resilient despite persistent inflationary pressures driven by strong consumer demand
Bifurcation in economy between upper- and lower-income groups; lower-income households experiencing difficulty keeping up with rising prices
Inflation moderated from peak but remains stubbornly high; services inflation persists while goods inflation is slowing
Insurance costs rising for most forms of business; technology costs increasing by up to 10% year-over-year in 2024
Housing prices remain restrictive for most consumers; builder costs continue rising due to labor and supply constraints
Labor markets remain tight especially for non-skilled and blue-collar workers; immigration helping to fill gaps
Wage increases moderating from 6-7% last year to 4-5% in 2024
why_it_matters: This CDIAC meeting summary provides ground-level intelligence on economic conditions from depository institution representatives across Federal Reserve Districts. The discussion highlights persistent inflation driven by labor costs and consumer demand, moderating goods inflation, housing affordability challenges, and labor market tightness—all relevant inputs for Fed policy assessment. The council's skepticism about near-term achievement of the 2% inflation target reflects sentiment in the broader business community. Note: This document represents regional anecdotes and perspectives from an advisory council, not official Fed policy statements.
macro_context: The document reflects regional economic conditions as of April 2024, showing persistent inflation, regional housing challenges, and labor market tightness. Council members expressed cautious optimism about the economic outlook, citing stable consumer confidence and slow return of small business capital investment. The bifurcation between upper- and lower-income households and the shift from goods to services inflation were highlighted as key developments. Source is historical (April 2024) and was truncated in provided text.
